Article Title: SC ends decades-old power tussle, Himachal to get 11,973 MU from Punjab, Haryana
Article Text:
The BBMB has been providing Himachal Pradesh with its 7.19 per cent share of electricity from these projects since November 1, 2011. However, Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the outstanding dues for the earlier period, amounting to 13,066 MU.

What was the 2011 Supreme Court verdict?

How did the dispute reach the Supreme Court?

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday settled a decades-old inter-state dispute over unpaid electricity dues from Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) projects, directing Punjab and Haryana to provide Himachal Pradesh with 11,973 million units (MU) of electricity over 20 years. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, accepted the Centre's proposal to clear the outstanding dues through an energy-based settlement instead of a cash payment.The settlement follows a 2011 Supreme Court verdict that recognised Himachal Pradesh's entitlement to a 7.19 per cent share in the electricity generated by the Bhakra Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects. The dues date back to 1966, but Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the state's outstanding share for the period before November 2011.Under the arrangement approved by the top court, Punjab and Haryana will provide the electricity over 20 years. The settlement also factors in an adjustment of around Rs 420 crore towards Himachal Pradesh's share of the historical capital costs incurred in building the dams. As a result, the hill state will not have to make any separate payment to Punjab or Haryana.The Centre had earlier proposed that the 13,066 MU in outstanding electricity dues be paid over 15 years, at the rate of 871 MU annually during the lean seasons between October and March. However, the states could not agree on the proposed timeline.Punjab initially opposed the 15-year arrangement and later sought to extend the payment period to 30 years. Himachal Pradesh, on the other hand, wanted the dues cleared within 10 years. The Supreme Court's decision to settle the matter over 20 years brings an end to the prolonged disagreement over the payment schedule.The original electricity arrears were calculated at 13,066 MU by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA). The Centre's proposal had also factored in Himachal Pradesh's liability towards the capital costs of the Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects.According to a report by PTI, the proposal says that Himachal Pradesh's liability was assessed at Rs 420.7 crore, comprising Rs 249.2 crore payable to Punjab and Rs 171.5 crore to Haryana. This represented the state's 7.19 per cent share of the composite of Punjab's outstanding loan-servicing costs for the projects since 1966-67.The Centre had suggested setting off this liability against a portion of the electricity arrears. At the proposed rate of Rs 3.85 per unit, around 1,093 MU would have been adjusted against the capital cost liability.The proposal also provided for the distribution of electricity arrears between Punjab and Haryana in the inter-state ratio of 58:42 for the Bhakra Nangal project and 60:40 for the Beas projects. However, since the states could not reach a consensus on the applicable electricity rate, the Centre recommended settling the dues in energy terms.The Supreme Court's 2011 decision fixed Himachal Pradesh's share in the BBMB projects at 7.19 per cent. Punjab's share was set at 51.80 per cent, while Haryana was allocated 37.51 per cent. Rajasthan's share largely remained unchanged, and Chandigarh's share was fixed at 3.50 per cent.The verdict also specified when Himachal Pradesh's entitlement would take effect for the three projects. The state was entitled to a share in the Bhakra project from November 1, 1966, the Dehar project from November 1977 and the Pong Dam project from January 1978.The BBMB has been providing Himachal Pradesh with its 7.19 per cent share of electricity from these projects since November 1, 2011, PTI reported, citing sources. However, Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the outstanding dues for the earlier period, amounting to 13,066 MU.The dispute dates back to the reorganisation of Punjab under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966. Himachal Pradesh maintained that, as a successor state, it was entitled to a 7.19 per cent share in the BBMB projects and their electricity generation.After efforts to resolve the disagreement between the neighbouring states failed, Himachal Pradesh approached the Supreme Court in 1996 through an original suit. It sought recognition of its entitlement to a share in the projects and the payment of the corresponding arrears.The Centre subsequently attempted to settle the matter outside court. However, with no agreement emerging between the states, the Supreme Court passed a decree on September 27, 2011, upholding Himachal Pradesh's 7.19 per cent entitlement.The latest order accepting the Centre's energy-based settlement provides a mechanism to clear the accumulated dues and closes a dispute that has remained unresolved for decades.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Monday settled a decades-old dispute over unpaid electricity dues from Bhakra Beas Management Board projects. Punjab and Haryana will provide Himachal Pradesh with 11,973 million units (MU) of electricity over 20 years. The dispute dates back to the reorganisation of Punjab under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966.

Article Title: OBC creamy layer row: SC protects past jobs, promotions but leaves pending cases open
Article Text:
The government has maintained that it is not challenging or seeking a review of the March 11 judgment.

Centre flags concerns over past recruitments

Dispute over salary-based creamy layer criteria

Centre seeks time to frame uniform mechanism

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday clarified that its March 11 ruling on determining the creamy layer status of Other Backward Class (OBC) candidates would not reopen completed appointments, promotions or seniority positions.The top court said cases that are still pending would be examined individually by the courts, based on their merits and the candidates' eligibility.A bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice R Mahadevan delivered the ruling while hearing an application filed by the Centre seeking clarity on how the March 11 judgment should be implemented. The Court also extended the deadline for compliance with its earlier directions by eight weeks.The clarification comes after the Centre raised concerns that applying the March 11 ruling retrospectively could unsettle years of government recruitments, service allocations and admissions to educational institutions.In its application, the government argued that applying the revised interpretation to past cases could affect appointments and admissions made under the rules and eligibility criteria in force at the time.It warned that this could create uncertainty over OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression.“Retrospective or belated application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the relevant time and may create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression. It may also affect admissions to Central and State educational institutions, universities and professional institutions. The Applicant therefore respectfully submits that the temporal operation of the Judgment requires clarification so as to avoid unsettling completed selections, appointments and admissions and the consequential rights arising therefrom”, the plea stated as per LiveLaw.The Centre said more than 5.69 lakh reserved vacancies, including 3.70 lakh OBC vacancies, were filled in Central government ministries, departments and their subordinate offices between 2016 and 2025.These recruitments were conducted under the August 8, 1993 Office Memorandum and subsequent government instructions.It argued that retrospective implementation could also necessitate a review of service allocations made through Civil Services Examinations since 2012. This could potentially lead to changes in the services and cadres allotted to officers already in government service, affecting their seniority and promotion prospects.The government also flagged possible complications in recruitment examinations conducted by the Railways, banks, Department of Posts and paramilitary organisations. It said similar disputes could arise in 18 States and Union Territories that follow the 1993 guidelines.The Centre further pointed out that candidates who become eligible for technical services several years after an examination might no longer meet the prescribed physical and medical standards. It also warned that reopening admissions granted to lakhs of students in universities and professional institutions could create difficulties, particularly where there are no provisions for additional seats.The clarification application stems from the Supreme Court's March 11 judgment on how the creamy layer among OBC candidates should be identified.The Court had ruled that a parent's salary alone cannot be used to determine whether an OBC candidate belongs to the creamy layer. The nature and category of the post held by the parents must also be taken into account.The dispute centred on two government instructions, the Office Memorandum issued on August 8, 1993, and a subsequent clarification dated October 14, 2004.The 1993 memorandum laid down the criteria for identifying the OBC creamy layer. It did not make a parent's salary the sole basis for exclusion from reservation benefits. Under the applicable Income/Wealth Test, salary and agricultural income are excluded from the income calculation, while the status and category of the parent's post remain relevant under the prescribed criteria.The 2004 clarification dealt with employees working in organisations such as public sector undertakings (PSUs), banks, universities and private companies, where the equivalence of their posts with government positions had not been established. It provided for consideration of parents' salary income in such cases.The Supreme Court held that the 2004 clarification could not introduce a new condition that was not part of the original 1993 policy. It also observed that treating children of PSU and private-sector employees differently from those of similarly placed government employees could amount to hostile discrimination and violate Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution, which guarantee equality before the law and equal opportunity in public employment.The government has maintained that it is not challenging or seeking a review of the March 11 judgment. Instead, it wants clarity on when the ruling should apply and how its directions should be implemented.The Centre has sought two years to consult stakeholders, establish equivalence between posts in non-government organisations and government positions, and develop a uniform mechanism for determining creamy-layer status in cases where such equivalence has not been established.It has also asked the SC not to disturb completed selections, appointments, service and cadre allocations, seniority positions and admissions made under the eligibility rules applicable at the time. The government has separately sought clarity on candidates who were already participating in examinations or recruitment processes when the March 11 judgment was delivered.In a separate interim application, the Centre sought permission to proceed with service allocation for 958 candidates recommended by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in the Civil Services Examination 2025, using the existing 1993 framework while the clarification application remained pending.The government argued that any further delay would push back the candidates' Foundation Course, training and induction schedules. It said the resulting disruption could not be reversed even if the Court eventually accepted its position.
Article Summary: The top court said cases that are still pending would be examined individually by the courts, based on their merits and the candidates' eligibility. The Court also extended the deadline for compliance with its earlier directions by eight weeks. The Centre raised concerns that applying the March 11 ruling retrospectively could unsettle years of government recruitments.

Article Title: IMA asks CBFC to deny certification to Sunny Deol-starrer, flags glorification of violence against doctors
Article Text:
The association said the objectionable content is the film's core theme and cannot be removed by mere excisions.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has urged the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) to refuse a certificate for the upcoming Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, starring Sunny Deol and Ravi Kishan, alleging that its teaser glorifies violence against doctors and hospital staff at a time when attacks on healthcare workers are a growing concern.In a detailed representation to the CBFC chairperson, the IMA said the film portrays a father who loses his daughter and takes revenge on those he holds responsible, with scenes showing him assaulting doctors and hospital staff inside a hospital. The association objected to dialogues in the teaser that accuse doctors of demanding excessive payments, ordering unnecessary tests and writing commission slips instead of prescriptions.The IMA argued that the film presents violence as a justified response to grievances against hospitals and could encourage attacks on medical professionals. It cited provisions of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, arguing that the content could incite offences, threaten public order and defame registered medical practitioners as a group.The representation comes against the backdrop of repeated attacks on healthcare workers.Citing a survey of 1,566 healthcare workers by experts from VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital and AIIMS, reported in May 2026, the IMA said 58.2 per cent felt unsafe at their workplace, and 78.4 per cent had faced threats while on duty. It also referred to an earlier IMA study that found more than 75 per cent of doctors had faced workplace violence.The association cited several incidents, including the killing of 22-year-old intern Dr Vandana Das in Kerala in May 2023, the assault on a doctor at Thamarassery in October 2025 and attacks on resident doctors in Aligarh in May 2026. It also referred to recent assaults in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.The IMA said violence against doctors disrupts medical services and creates fear among healthcare workers, affecting patients as well. Citing Supreme Court observations on the issue, it has urged the CBFC to deny certification to the film and its promotional material if they depict violence against healthcare workers or portray doctors as corrupt. Alternatively, it has sought referral to a Revising Committee, a screening for IMA representatives and a medical expert, and removal of scenes that glorify or justify such violence. The association has also sought a hearing before the Board decides, citing the film’s scheduled nationwide release on November 20.
Article Summary: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has urged the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) to refuse a certificate for the upcoming Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak. The association said the film portrays a father who loses his daughter and takes revenge on those he holds responsible, with scenes showing him assaulting doctors and hospital staff inside a hospital.

NEW DELHI: Referring to the contradictory orders given by Supreme Court in the matter of bail to the accused on the ground of delay in trial and long incarceration for UAPA offences, which have been referred to a larger bench for authoritative pronouncement, former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases.The accused submitted that two co-accused, including Tasleem Ahmed, were granted bail by SC on the grou-nd that determination of the issues by the larger bench would take time, and they could not be made to suffer continued incarceration.Seeking parity with the co-accused, Sharjeel Imam, who has already spent six years and nine months in custody, said in his petition, filed through advocate Fauzia Shakil, that two co-accused in the same FIR were released on interim bail by the court on May 22 under a principle which applies to him in greater degree.The accused moved SC after their plea for bail was rejected by the trial court and Delhi High Court on the ground that the apex court had purportedly set a deadline of Jan 5, 2027, for them to file a bail petition.The petition asked "whether the principle recognised by this Court in Tasleem Ahmed v. State order dated 22.05.2026, that an accused cannot be made to suffer continued incarceration merely because an important question of law has arisen for authoritative settlement, can be withheld from the petitioner alone by reference to the role attributed to him, when the question referred to concerns the correctness of the very judgment which declined his bail and relief in Tasleem Ahmed case was granted without any examination of role?"It further argued, "Whether liberty reserved by this Court in a judgment declining bail, to renew the prayer for bail at a defined point, operates as a bar upon the statutory jurisdiction of the Special Court and of the High Court to consider an application for bail founded on supervening circumstances be-fore that point, when the same paragraph of the judgment holds that pre-trial detention cannot be permitted to continue without regard to the progress of the trial and that Article 21 operates as a continuing check against continued incarceration without substantial progress of the trial?"
Article Summary: Former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases. The accused submitted that two co-accused, including Tasleem Ahmed, were granted bail by SC on the grou-nd that determination of the issues by the larger bench would take time.

Article Title: Centre eases immigration rules for Pakistani, Afghan minorities and other foreign nationals
Article Text:
The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan.

NEW DELHI: The Union home ministry has relaxed passport and visa requirements for several categories of foreign nationals residing in India, including Pakistani citizens who entered prior to December 31, 2009 with the intention to permanently reside in India but could not renew their Pakistani passport due to non-possession of computerised nationality identity card issued by Pakistan government.Other categories of foreign nationals for whom passport and visa rules have been eased as part of the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) ORder, 2026, include citizens of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan belonging to their religious minorities; Sri Lankan Tamil refugees and Tibetans.The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan, allowing them to enter or exit India by producing any one of the documents specified in the visa manual; However, in case they are entering or exiting India from or to a place other than Nepal or Bhutan, they must in possession of a valid passport. Nepal and Bhutan citizens who have embarked at or transited through China Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan, must be in possession of both a valid passport and valid visa.The requirement of a valid passport and visa would also not apply to a male member of the Muslim community, being originally an Indian citizen, who went to Pakistan after partition between August 15, 1947 and Dec 31, 1965 leaving behind family in India and returned to India on or before Dec 31, 2009, and settled in Keralam on a valid Pakistani passport but which has since expired or been lost.However, such a person should not have married or acquired immoveable property while in Pakistan; ,while going to Pakistan, left behind family members who are Indian citizens; shall not return to Pakistan; and should not have any adverse report from the police or security agencies.A citizen of India entering into India from Nepal or Bhutan or departing from India to Nepal or Bhutan by land or air shall produce before the immigration officer one of the documents specified in the visa manual to establish their identity, though this exemption would not be applicable if departing to or returning from countries other than Nepal or Bhutan through the Indo-Nepal or Indo-Bhutan border of by air. In all such cases, a valid passport will be required and the exit and entry into India shall be only through the designated immigration points.The provisions in the Act and rules with regard to requirement of valid passport or other valid travel document and valid visa for entry into, stay in and exit from India, shall also not apply for a member of naval, military or air forces of India, entering into or exiting from India on duty and members of the family of any such person when accompanying him on a government transport; registered Sri Lankan Tamil nationals who have taken shelter in India up to Jan 9, 2015; as well as the foreign crew of foreign military vessels coming for repairs in India who are granted military ship repair permits by the immigration officer, provided they hold their military identification documents.Exempted categories include a Tibetan who has entered India after 1959 but before May 30,, 2003 on an entry permit issued by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu; or who entered after May 30, 2003, on the special entry permit issued through the designated immigration post on the Indo-Nepal border and a certificate of registration was issued by the registration officer concerned.Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Christian, Jain and Parsi citizens of Pakistan who entered India before Dec 31, 2024, fearing religious persecution in their home country, without valid documents including passport or other travel documents; or with valid documents including passport that has since expired, would also get relief under the amended Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) order. However, such a person shall be required to obtain an appropriate category of visa after their entry into India, for continued stay.Also exempt now from requirement of a valid passport and visa are persons of Indian origin who subsequently acquired the citizenship of Malaysia or Singapore and returned to India on or before Dec 31, 2009 on a valid passport issued by either of those countries, which has since expired and is not being renewed by those countries because such person does not meet the conditions specified by those countries. Such persons must have documentary proof that they are a person of Indian origin.
Article Summary: The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan. Pakistani citizens who entered prior to December 31, 2009 could not renew their Pakistani passport due to non-possession of computerised nationality identity card. Other categories of foreign nationals for whom passport and visa rules have been eased include citizens of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan belonging to their religious minorities.

Article Title: EC rejigs work, new officer to oversee ECINet functioning
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has reallocated work among its deputy election commissioners (DEC) and directors-general in view of the recent appointment of DEC Prakash Rajpurohit. DG (IT) Seema Khanna, who heads the division that manages the ECINet portal and application, will now put up all files regarding the IT/ICT and grievances divisions under her charge through senior DEC Pawan Kumar Sharma Sources in the commission said Khanna - whose name cropped up after Indian Express reported on Sept 23, 2026, that election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected to the alleged "centralisation" of ECINET, with access restricted for even authorised field officers - was earlier putting up these files through senior DEC Maneesh Garg, and before that through then DEC Sanjay Kumar.Though Garg had, while officiating as DEC (administration) during the leave period of DEC Bhanu Prakash Yeturu in July, issued a work allocation order that allowed Khanna to no longer route her files through then DEC Sanjay Kumar, this order was never implemented after the two election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected. This is recorded in the affidavit filed recently by EC in the Supreme Court."The work redistribution orders issued by the officer concerned were never implemented after the orders of the two commissioners, and the oversight of the IT division by the DEC was never actually withdrawn," EC said in the affidavit issued with approval of the full commission.Khanna, as a result, continued routing files through Sanjay Kumar, and after his stint with Election Commission ended, through Kumar's link officer Maneesh Garg.Under the work reallocation order dated Nov 4, Pawan Kumar Sharma will be the new deputy election commissioner in-charge of the IT/ICT as well as grievance/PGRS divisions, and Khanna would put up files of these divisions through him.Sandhu and Joshi had written separate letters to cabinet secretary T V Somanathan in July end, complaining about the working of senior Garg. In the near-identical letters, they said that Garg, soon after assuming charge as link officer of then DEC (administration) Yeturu, who was on leave, had issued an order regarding work allocation among senior DECs, DGs and equivalent officers, without discussing the revised allocation with the commission or the two election commissioners.This, Sandhu and Joshi said, was despite repeated oral instructions to all officers concerned against taking such actions without prior approval of the commission.The cabinet secretary had merely forwarded the election commissioners' letter to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, apart from sending an acknowledgement to the two commissioners. As per the file noting furnished by the cabinet secretariat in reply to an RTI application by Commodore Lokesh Batra (Retd), it was stated that any action against Garg "at this stage may be inappropriate" as the letters were not sent by the commission as a whole. "It may also be construed as interference in the functioning of the constitutional body," it was stated.
Article Summary: The Election Commission has reallocated work among its deputy election commissioners (DEC) and directors-general. DG (IT) Seema Khanna, who heads the division that manages the ECINet portal and application, will now put up all files regarding the IT/ICT and grievances divisions through senior DEC Pawan Kumar Sharma.

NEW DELHI: The Centre told Supreme Court on Thursday that it is considering appointing a committee to review provisions of the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026, the operation of which was stayed by SC saying its provisions could fuel divisions in society.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that govt was contemplating setting up an expert panel to revisit provisions of the regulations to ensure that "nobody has any apprehension or anyone is left dissatisfied".The move appears to be aimed at assuaging the "hurt" among upper castes over having been excluded from among those who can complain against caste abuse ahead of polls in UP and Uttarakhand.Upper castes, a vocal constituency and an influential part of BJP's social base, argue that the "equity guidelines" framed at SC's instance, does not take into account the changed socio-economic conditions which have seen dominance shift to the newly-empowered OBCs, and would leave them vulnerable to harassment.CJI Surya Kant said the provisions must ensure that "concerns of every student, the next generation and the young generation are addressed" appropriately.The SC adjourned hearing on a batch of petitions, including one filed by the mothers of Rohith Vemula and Payal Tadvi who committed suicide allegedly after failing to endure caste-based discrimination on college campuses.Mehta said govt shared SC's concerns and intends to revisit the provisions of the 2026 regulations. The same bench of CJI Kant and Justice Bagchi had on Jan 29 kept in abeyance the controversial regulations taking exception to several provisions.
Article Summary: The move appears to be aimed at assuaging the "hurt" among upper castes over having been excluded from among those who can complain against caste abuse ahead of polls in UP and Uttarakhand. The SC adjourned hearing on a batch of petitions, including one filed by the mothers of Rohith Vemula and Payal Tadvi who committed suicide.

Article Title: Oversight layer intact, says EC official after poll panel tweaks work order for IT chief Seema Khanna
Article Text:
Why was Seema Khanna's role under scrutiny?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday said there is no change in the supervisory authority to which its director general of information technology Seema Khanna reports.The clarification came a day after the panel issued a fresh work allocation placing Khanna under the charge of deputy election commissioner Prakash Raj Purohit instead of senior deputy EC Manish Garg.A controversy had erupted after Garg issued an order on July 28 asking Khanna to report directly to the Election Commission, comprising Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Vivek Joshi and SS Sandhu.Garg had issued the order after deputy EC Sanjay Kumar, to whom Khanna had been reporting, was transferred to the Delhi government. The change effectively removed an intermediary layer of oversight, allowing Khanna to report directly to the Election Commission.ECs Sandhu and Joshi objected to the order and subsequently wrote separate letters to cabinet secretary TV Somanathan, raising concerns over the distribution of responsibilities.The order was then put in abeyance. The EC also told the Supreme Court that the July 28 work allocation order was never implemented.Asked whether Khanna had reported directly to the Commission between July 28 and November 4, without an added layer of a reporting boss in the form of a deputy EC, an election official on Thursday said: "Since the order was not implemented, Khanna was supervised by Garg after Sanjay Kumar moved out of the EC. Now, she will report to Raj Purohit, who joined as deputy EC a few days ago."Garg was the "link officer" for Kumar, which meant that Kumar's assigned tasks were transferred to Garg after he left the Election Commission.Khanna's role had come under scrutiny amid concerns over the functioning of the electoral roll software and the exercise of powers by Electoral Registration Officers (EROs).According to a report by The Indian Express, the two Election Commissioners were concerned that field-level officers, who are legally responsible for preparing electoral rolls, were unable to perform certain functions because the software did not permit them to do so.The permissions required to carry out these functions were reportedly controlled by the EC's IT division, headed by Khanna.The commissioners repeatedly raised concerns that powers legally vested in EROs were being increasingly centralised through the EC's IT system, potentially restricting the authority of officers responsible for preparing and revising electoral rolls.
Article Summary: The Election Commission says there is no change in the supervisory authority to which Seema Khanna reports. The clarification came a day after the panel issued a fresh work allocation placing Khanna under the charge of a deputy election commissioner. A controversy had erupted after Garg issued an order on July 28 asking Khanna to report directly to the Election Commission.

Article Title: ‘Vote gone, rights gone’: Rahul alleges BJP conspiracy in schemes linked with voter ID instead of Aadhaar
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi alleges voter ID-welfare link part of BJP’s ‘conspiracy’

Rahul Gandhi accuses Centre of linking welfare benefits to voter lists amid SIR row

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Centre over Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh's announcement that voter ID cards would be used instead of Aadhaar to identify beneficiaries of social welfare programmes under the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.Calling the move a "conspiracy", the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha alleged that linking welfare benefits to voter IDs could put people's access to government schemes at risk.In a post on X, Rahul claimed that the announcement was part of a wider attempt to remove names from electoral rolls through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). He alleged that millions of names were being deleted under the exercise and that those most critical of the BJP were being targeted."Modi government minister's announcement - Benefits of schemes will now be determined not by Aadhaar, but by Voter ID. The conspiracy runs very deep—take your time to understand it. Under the guise of SIR, millions of names are being struck off voter lists—if not stopped, even more will be removed. Whose names are being targeted the most? Those who are furious with the BJP," Rahul said.He also accused the Election Commission of India (ECI) of colluding with the BJP, alleging that electoral rolls were no longer being maintained by an impartial body.Rahul named Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of being a "Modi government employee" and claiming that his alleged collusion with the BJP in "vote theft" had been exposed with evidence."The preparation is underway to craft such a list where the majority is always BJP's—and now that very list will decide whether you get scheme benefits or not. Anyone who decided yesterday that the BJP must go—will have their names cherry-picked and struck off. Name struck—vote gone. Vote gone—rights gone. And just like that, you'll become invisible citizens of a hijacked democracy—where the people don't elect the government, the government selects its people," he added.Rahul further warned that making voter ID mandatory for welfare benefits could eventually affect access to ration, pensions, MGNREGA wages, housing assistance, scholarships and reservations. He argued that voting rights should not be made a condition for receiving welfare benefits."Today, Panchayati Raj schemes. Tomorrow, rations? Pensions? MGNREGA? Housing? Scholarships? Reservations? This isn't politics to win elections—it's an arrangement to steal elections and a permanent setup to cling to power.Voting is your right, not a condition. A poor person's pension cannot be enslaved to their voter card. This isn't just vote theft—it's rights theft. We won't let this happen," he said.Singh, also known as Lallan Singh, had announced that beneficiaries seeking financial assistance and welfare payments under schemes of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj would need to provide an Elector's Photo Identity Card (EPIC) number and undergo mandatory biometric authentication. Article Title: ‘Hope you are enjoying Delhi weather’: CJI blames vehicles as SC takes up air pollution case
Article Text:
Supreme Court flags traffic, stubble burning in Delhi-NCR

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday heard a suo motu case concerning air pollution in Delhi-NCR, with Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant expressing concern over rising pollution levels and stressing the need for measures to tackle vehicular emissions and stubble burning A bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard submissions from senior advocate Aparajita Singh, the amicus curiae in the matter, and the Centre's counsel.CJI Kant opened the hearing with the remark according to Live Law, "We hope all of you are enjoying Delhi weather." Singh responded that pollution levels were hovering around the severe category and said, "we are losing our voice as well. It's like smoking 30 cigarettes a day!"The CJI observed that pollution levels had fallen because it had rained in Delhi. Singh told the court that stubble burning contributed 14 per cent to pollution on November 5, but stressed that the national capital was already polluted before farm fires added to the problem."Transport is the biggest problem," she said, adding that authorities needed to focus on local sources of pollution as well as stubble burning. She pointed to transport, energy and waste burning as key concerns across the National Capital Region (NCR).On stubble management, the CJI said that the sowing season for farmers was under way and that stubble burning should have stopped. Singh, however, said farmers faced difficulties even when equipment was provided to them."To farmers, even if you give equipment, they don't have fuel. Price of fuel this year I don't have to highlight. Secondly, it does not work in small farms," she told the bench.Also read: Delhi air quality worsens, AQI hits 389 as several areas turn ‘severe’; GRAP-II measures underway Justice Bagchi referred to a proposal by authorities to acquire stubble at a fixed rate. The CJI suggested that the procurement rate should be announced in advance and that machinery should be provided to gram panchayats, as individual farmers could not afford the cost of such equipment."This machine needs to be given to Gram Panchayat. Individuals cannot afford. This is how machine can work. Cost of machine itself," the CJI said.The court also discussed the possibility of creating storage facilities for collected stubble. The CJI said that warehousing could provide an additional source of income for those involved in the process. The Additional Solicitor General (ASG) said a scheme was already in place and agreed to raise the suggestions with the Agriculture Ministry.The ASG told the bench that the government had taken several measures to address stubble burning and that farm fires had reduced significantly this year, particularly in Haryana. He also referred to financial incentives introduced by the state.Turning to vehicular pollution, the ASG said measures included phasing out diesel-operated rickshaws and mandating buses from other cities entering Delhi. The CJI, however, stressed that traffic congestion on roads connecting Delhi with the NCR remained a major concern."Major cause is vehicular pollution. Look at the roads in Delhi, connecting to NCR. The kind of bumper to bumper vehicles are going," the CJI said.He also flagged the lack of adequate public transport. The ASG said significant progress had been made in this area and that the authorities were considering immediate and intermediate measures.Singh pointed out that an earlier court order concerning toll plazas had not been fully implemented. She said vehicles were being stopped at NCR borders and made to idle, adding to pollution. The ASG conceded that implementation of the order was incomplete.The bench also discussed the impact of seasonal weather conditions on pollution levels. Singh said smoke disperses during summer but remains trapped during winter.The CJI called for greater awareness of traditional practices and questioned why people could not return to their original customs. Singh said that reverting to the use of diyas during Diwali would be ideal, while highlighting that poorer sections of society were among those most affected by pollution.The CJI observed that the Diwali period was also an important source of livelihood for poorer people, but said those who could afford to make firecrackers a social status symbol were contributing to the problem."Poor people do not generate any pollution. They are the sufferers. It is those who can afford it and those who can contribute to it,” the CJI remarked.The ASG said Delhi's geographical location made it difficult for smoke to disperse. The CJI then questioned whether scientific methods had been adopted to address the problem, observing that other measures had been "Tried and failed tools".The ASG said the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) regulated activities according to pollution levels, adding that Delhi attracted people from across the country and that every activity generated pollution. "We are only doing management," he said.The CJI pointed to the city's high pollution levels, remarking, "it's already touching 400!"Meanwhile, Delhi continued to reel under high pollution levels on Friday. The city's overall Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 389 in the 'very poor' category at 8 am, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).Several monitoring stations recorded AQI levels in the 'severe' category. IIT Delhi and Rohini reported an AQI of 474 each, followed by Punjabi Bagh at 465, RK Puram at 443, ITO at 422, Firoz Shah Road at 420 and India Gate at 403.Other areas also recorded high pollution levels, with Anand Vihar and Akshardham reporting an AQI of 359. IGI Airport Terminal 3 recorded 385, while the readings stood at 393 in Aya Nagar and 391 in Chandni Chowk.Municipal authorities deployed truck-mounted water sprinklers around India Gate as part of water-sprinkling operations under Stage II of the GRAP.According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Delhi recorded a minimum temperature of 17.8 degrees Celsius on Friday morning, with mainly clear skies. The weather department forecast shallow fog over the next four days, followed by fog or mist during the early morning hours of November 10 and 11.Residents continued to report discomfort amid the deteriorating air quality.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Friday heard a suo motu case concerning air pollution in Delhi-NCR. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant expressed concern over rising pollution levels. He stressed the need for measures to tackle vehicular emissions and stubble burning. The court discussed the possibility of creating storage facilities for collected stubble.

Article Title: Up to 10-fold statutory costs, month-long delays: Report flags hurdles in used vehicle transfers
Article Text:
Vehicle transfers cost up to 10x statutory fees; UP, Bihar and Bengal ranked worst on the Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index 2026.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Vehicle ownership transfers can cost up to 10 times the statutory fees, with total expenses, including agent charges, in the range of Rs 13,000-14,000 in parts of Bihar, Rs 7,000-8,000 in Tamil Nadu and Rs 5,000-8,000 in Uttar Pradesh, according to the Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index 2026 released by a consumer rights advocacy organisation and a startup industry body.The report, prepared by Consumer Voice and IndiaTech on the basis of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, transport policies of 15 states and interviews with automobile dealers, RTO agents and vehicle owners, has exposed the sharp gap between reforms initiated by the Centre and ground realities in states in terms of their actual implementation.The report found that the all-inclusive cost of an RC transfer, including agent charges, is the lowest in Kerala (Rs 500-2,400), followed by Karnataka (Rs 2,000-2,500), Andhra Pradesh (Rs 3,000-3,500) and Delhi (Rs 3,000-3,600). The time taken to complete a transfer also varies widely — as little as a week in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana but more than a month in Uttar Pradesh.The study assessed ownership transfer procedures across 15 states accounting for more than 85% of India’s organised pre-owned car market. It found Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Delhi to be top performers in ease of vehicle ownership while Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal were placed at the bottom of the list.The report highlighted how unofficial expenses, procedural inefficiencies and dependence on intermediaries continue to inflate the cost of transferring vehicle ownership. Nearly 100% of respondents surveyed said they had relied on agents to complete the transfer process. “Reducing these hidden transaction costs will be critical for improving accessibility, accelerating market formalisation and enhancing the overall ease of vehicle ownership,” it said.None of the states figured in the ‘high ease’ or excellent category, with Andhra Pradesh, the top-ranked state, scoring only 5.9 on a scale of 0-10. Kerala scored 5.7, followed by Tamil Nadu and Delhi at 4.6 each. Rajasthan (4) and Haryana (3.9) were also in the lower half of the rankings, while West Bengal (2.6), Bihar (2.5) and Uttar Pradesh (2.5) brought up the rear.The report comes at a time when India’s pre-owned vehicle market is expanding rapidly and projected to grow from $36.4 billion in 2025 to over $73.5 billion by 2030. The market has already overtaken new vehicle sales in volume. However, fragmented state-level rules, incomplete digitisation and cumbersome procedures continue to impede seamless vehicle ownership transfers.It also found that 39% of respondents had reported delays in receiving their registration certificates after completing vehicle transfers, while 61.5% were unaware of the requirement of party peshi until they reached the RTO. As many as 63% could not accurately estimate the total cost of completing an ownership transfer, reflecting widespread opacity in transaction charges.
Article Summary: Vehicle ownership transfers can cost up to 10 times the statutory fees. Total expenses, including agent charges, in the range of Rs 13,000-14,000 in parts of Bihar. Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Delhi were top performers in ease of vehicle ownership. Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal were placed at the bottom of the list.

NEW DELHI: Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a Rs 14,500 crore viability gap funding (VGF) scheme to develop 92 gigawatt-hour (GWh) of grid-scale energy storage capacity by FY31 to facilitate integration of large-scale renewable energy generation.Power ministry officials said the scheme will support the creation of additional storage capacity equivalent to 170% of the existing 54 GWh available in India. Article Title: Aadhaar verification goes paperless as UIDAI brings 300 entities on board

NEW DELHI: Checking into a hotel, entering a hospital or verifying the identity of a gig worker could increasingly be done without submitting photocopies of Aadhaar cards. The Unique Identification Authority of India ( UIDAI ) has brought 300 organisations on board its offline verification system since January, expanding the use of consent-based digital identity checks across everyday services.The development comes as the Aadhaar App gains popularity, with nearly 7.5 crore downloads and more than 86 lakh people using it to update their registered mobile numbers without visiting an Aadhaar centre.The 300 organisations, registered as Offline Verification Seeking Entities (OVSEs), cover sectors such as hospitality, healthcare, education, events, the gig economy and consumer services. The initiative is intended to replace physical document collection with digital verification, reducing paperwork and the risk of personal information being misused.Under the system, residents can share their identity details through the Aadhaar App after giving consent. They can choose whether to share complete or selected information, while their 12-digit Aadhaar number is not transferred to the organisation conducting the verification. The process does not require the organisation to connect to UIDAI’s central identity database.The expansion follows UIDAI’s earlier efforts to encourage hotels, government departments and other service providers to accept app-based Aadhaar credentials instead of routinely collecting photocopies.In April, UIDAI had reported onboarding its first 100 entities.Alongside the verification initiative, the Aadhaar App is increasingly being used for updating personal details. According to UIDAI, residents have completed 22.16 lakh address updates and 40.25 lakh email updates through the application.Security-related features have also seen substantial use. The app has recorded 4.6 crore biometric lock and unlock transactions, allowing users to control access to their fingerprint and iris-based authentication. Another 3.61 lakh Aadhaar lock and unlock transactions have been recorded.The growing use of these features is significant as Aadhaar moves beyond government welfare delivery to routine identity verification in private services. The emphasis is now on allowing residents to prove their identity without unnecessarily disclosing personal information.UIDAI said the expansion aligns with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act’s emphasis on consent and limiting data collection, while making Aadhaar-related services more accessible through smartphones.
Article Summary: Unique Identification Authority of India has brought 300 organisations on board its offline verification system. The initiative is intended to replace physical document collection with digital verification, reducing paperwork and the risk of personal information being misused. Development comes as the Aadhaar App gains popularity, with nearly 7.5 crore downloads.

Article Title: Centre amends Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order: What Indians travelling to or returning from Nepal or Bhutan need to know
Article Text:
Citizens of Nepal or Bhutan entering or leaving India

Who all are exempted

What is a 'visa manual'

NEW DELHI: The ministry of home affairs (MHA) on Thursday notified the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) Order, 2026, introducing specific amendments to the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order, 2025.Under the amended order, Indian nationals travelling to or returning from Nepal or Bhutan by land or air will be required to produce any one of the identity documents specified in the visa manual before an immigration officer. They will also have to furnish any information sought by the officer.The exemption provided under this clause shall not apply to a citizen of India departing to or returning from countries other than Nepal or Bhutan through the Indo-Nepal or Indo-Bhutan border by land or by air. In all such cases, they shall be required to possess a valid passport and their exit from or entry into India shall be only through the designated immigration posts.Under the new order, citizens of Nepal and Bhutan entering or leaving India by land or air will also be required to produce any one of the identity documents specified in the visa manual before an immigration officer. They will also have to provide any information sought by the officer.However, this exemption will not apply to citizens of Nepal or Bhutan entering or leaving India from or to a country other than Nepal or Bhutan.The exemption will also not apply to those who have boarded a flight or transited through China, Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan. In such cases, they must possess both a valid passport and a valid visa.In both cases, citizens of Nepal and Bhutan must possess a valid passport and a valid visa.The order also specifies categories of people exempted from the requirements to possess a valid passport or other travel document and visa for entering, staying in or exiting India.(a) Members of the Indian Navy, Army and Air Force travelling to or from India on official duty. Their family members accompanying them on government transport are also covered.(b) Registered Sri Lankan Tamil nationals who took shelter in India on or before January 9, 2015. They must be registered with an officer designated by the Central or state government.(c) Foreign crew members of military vessels, including warships and other government ships operated for non-commercial purposes, visiting India for repairs. They must have a Military Ship Repair Permit issued by an immigration officer at a designated immigration post and carry valid military identity documents.(d) Tibetans who entered India after 1959 but before May 30, 2003, with an Entry Permit issued by the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu. The exemption also covers Tibetans who entered India after May 30, 2003 through a Special Entry Permit issued by the embassy and through a designated immigration post on the India-Nepal border.(e) Members of minority communities — Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians — from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who were forced to seek shelter in India due to religious persecution or fear of persecution, provided they entered India on or before December 31, 2024.The order defined the document as a manual issued by the central government from time to time, containing instructions on visas, immigration and related matters.
Article Summary: Citizens of Nepal and Bhutan entering or leaving India by land or air will also be required to produce any one of the identity documents specified in the visa manual. Members of minority communities — Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians — from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan are also exempted.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Travis Kelce wanted his $5.35 million Ohio mansion to become a private escape from the spotlight. Instead, his plans to reshape the historic estate have sparked growing tension in Bratenahl. Neighbours fear that introducing extensive greenery and altering the property's surroundings could trigger problems that extend well beyond the mansion's boundaries. The concerns have put the couple's renovation plans under fresh scrutiny.The biggest concern among residents centres on the property's landscaping plans. Adding rows of evergreen trees might improve privacy, but neighbours worry that the changes could have consequences for the natural surroundings.Katherine Bolton, who has lived next to the property for more than 30 years, raised concerns about planting trees close to underground infrastructure. She told the Bratenahl Architectural Review Board that the shared sewer line dates back approximately 115 years.Her warning highlighted a problem that can develop slowly before becoming expensive to fix."When you plant that many trees from a short distance from a sewer line, you're going to have a problem in the future," Bolton said, according to Cleveland 19.She also revealed that she had received a $75,000 estimate for lining the ageing pipe to protect it against possible root intrusion.The concern is not simply about the trees themselves. Root growth can affect underground structures, while changes to established vegetation can also influence the local environment. However, no future damage has been confirmed.Kelce and Swift's representatives have already taken steps to address some of the complaints. Property manager Patrick Hyland told officials that the couple had spent $7,500 repairing a damaged section of the shared sewer line. The original eight-foot design was reduced to six feet and moved inside the property boundary. Additional gates were included to maintain access and address residents' concerns.Neighbour Chuck Bauernschmidt also questioned the removal of existing vegetation and raised concerns about wildlife."I live here, been here for 47 years. I take offense when we start knocking trees down," he said.Meanwhile, officials questioned whether the proposed rear-yard trees would exceed Bratenahl's 10-foot height restriction.The board approved the front landscaping, but the rear plans remained unresolved. A further review was scheduled for November 10.For Kelce and Swift, the challenge is becoming bigger than improving privacy.
